title: Sketching with Patches of Tone
content: In this graphite pencil sketch, Charles Bargue (1825–83) uses well placed patches of tone rather than using only outlines to describe the form.Charles Bargue, graphite, 8 x 5 3/16 inches,Metropolitan MuseumThe patches are made out of short, parallel strokes, which create an impressionistic, painterly effect, even though he's working only in unblended pencil.Charles Bargue helped create theDrawing Courseused in many ateliers.The method of sketching with patches of tonal values is also described inSketching - from Square One to Trafalgar Squareand Ernest Watson'sThe Art of Pencil Drawing.Previous post:The El Dorado Page(Ernest Watson)
